name: Threshold Dimension
definition: The **Threshold dimension** of a family $\mathcal{H}$, denoted by $T(\mathcal{H})$, is the largest integer $d$ such that there exists a set $S\subset \mathcal{X}$, of size $d$ such that $\mathcal{H}\_{|S}$ contains thresholds, i.e. there is an ordering $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ of the elements of $S$ such that $$ \forall 0\le k\le d,\, \{x_1,\ldots,x_k\} \in \mathcal{H}\_{|S}\,. $$
comments: Note that this means $\mathcal{H}\_{|S}$ contains a $d+1$-chain, i.e. $d+1$ sets $S_1,\ldots,S_{d+1}$ such that $S_1\subset \ldots\subset S_{d+1}$.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

monotonic.proof: A threshold witness contained in a subfamily remains contained in the larger class.

p_monotonic.proof: A threshold witness in a projection is already realized by the original class on those coordinates.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Counterexample to strict c-monotonicity: for $\mathcal H=\{0001,0010,0011,0100,0111,1001\}$, conditioning the third coordinate gives two fibres of threshold dimension 2, while $\mathrm T(\mathcal H)=2$.
